title: `ia host` applies the generated agents, skills and `@hook` groups through the one projection writer, and its receipt lists them
summary: @inventarch/cli: `ia host <claude|codex>` and `ia init --host` render the position packet together with the files and hooks generated from the workspace's authored records, computed once, and apply exactly that set through the one projection writer: for claude one .claude/agents/<name>.md per authored `@agent-profile` and one .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md per authored `@playbook`, each with the packet marker, and one hook group per authored `@hook` in .claude/settings.local.json; for codex one .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md per playbook, every profile and hook reported as not taken. One apply retires a 1.x steward guard, then registers or removes the hook groups against the payload `ia host` materializes and verifies, then writes the files, then the receipt. `ia host <host> --remove --apply` no longer requires an admitting workspace or records that open: it renders nothing and removes the registration, its hook groups and its files whatever the records say. A record renamed or deleted takes its obsolete agent file, skill or group away on the next apply; unrelated settings keys and groups and unmarked files are kept; a second apply changes no file, setting or state and writes the same receipt rows. `ia project`, the install, update and remove refresh and a migration keep the groups an earlier `ia host` registration owns in step with the records, against the payload that registration recorded, writing nothing and not reading that payload while the owned hooks and selections are the declared ones, and refusing at that payload, naming `ia host claude --apply`, when a change needs it and it is gone or changed; with no registration they register none and list each declared hook as not taken. The receipt gains generated (record identity, word, path and SHA-256 of each generated file), definitions (each authored `@operation` with its handler and validator ids copied as authored and never resolved or run, and each `@harness` with the agents, skills and hooks it registers, as that apply wrote and registered them: a hook it did not register, for want of a payload, is not listed), hooks (each owned group by `@hook` identity, the tools the hook declares and the group's SHA-256) and unsupported (each authored record the host does not take, with the reason); removedHooks lists each hook group an apply removed, by `@hook` identity and the SHA-256 it was last registered with, an interrupted earlier apply's included; removed also lists the generated files an apply deleted; a receipt without these sections still reads. An install, update or remove plans the refresh's files and hook step before its first install write, and `ia init --migrate` checks the hook step before it plans: an owned hook group deleted, changed or duplicated by hand, a recorded payload a change of hooks would need, or a generated skill refused at a populated folder of the user's refuses there, never after the install commits, and the install preview lists a generated agent as the refresh writes it, never as a 1.x file to remove. Where disableAllHooks turns hooks off, no group is written: a group already owned for a hook still declared stays registered; an obsolete owned group is removed, or, when the payload the kept groups were registered against is gone, kept and reported as kept (never as registered) until hooks are back on or that payload is materialized again; a group deleted, changed or duplicated by hand refuses as it does with hooks on; and each authored hook with no group is reported as not taken, naming the settings file, while the MCP entry, the packet, the agents and the skills apply as before (a 2.0.0 apply did not refuse there either). The plans of `ia host` and `ia project` list each hook group's action (create, update, unchanged or remove) and each record not taken. A generation refusal keeps its own code and names ia validate. `ia doctor` adds a row for each owned hook group that is missing (deleted by hand) or modified (changed or duplicated): a fail whose remedy is `ia host claude --remove --apply`, after which `ia host claude --apply` registers the workspace's hooks again, since apply never puts back a group the user took away; a guard group naming --hook that no registration owns is a warning, left in place; an authored `@hook` the last apply could not register is a warning saying it guards nothing, naming `ia host claude --apply`; and an outdated row when the generated rows differ from the receipt's, a receipt written before generation included. @inventarch/distribution: the ./projection subpath exports GENERATED_PATHS and projectionOwnable(host, path). The planner owns generated files at .claude/agents/<name>.md, .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md through the same ia.host-projection-state.v1 state: an owned one no render writes any more is removed when it still carries an owned marker (a listed skill without one is kept as foreign), along with the skill folder that removal empties (never recursively), a generated skill is refused where its folder already holds files the state does not own, an unmarked or hand-edited file at a generated path is refused and never overwritten or removed, a generated agent is refused (IA-DIST-PATH-UNSAFE) where .claude/agents is a link, and a generated agent at the path of an owned 1.x steward file replaces it as one update, never an update and a remove of the same path. @inventarch/steward-hook: projection protection reads a state that lists generated skills and protects them, as it protects generated agents. Limits: ownership stays in the projection and hook ownership states, never the receipt; Codex agents and hooks remain unsupported; a 2.0.0 CLI cannot plan a workspace this release applied a generated set to until the registration is removed (see the state-evolution note).
